problems.title: Match total indices in a geometric progression
problems.question: In a geometric progression b₁₄b₂₃=b₇bₖ. Find k.
problems.idea: Products with equal index sums have equal total powers of the common ratio.
steps: The left side is b₁²q³⁵. The right side is b₁²q^(k+5).
For a nonzero, nonconstant progression with a positive ratio other than 1, equal powers give 35=k+5.
Thus k=30, which makes the identity hold for every geometric progression.
problems.answer: k=30 as the general index identity.
problems.note: A particular degenerate progression can allow other indices: for q=1 every k works; for q=-1 any even k works. A unique k needs the usual nondegeneracy assumption.

problems.title: A zero odd partial sum fixes the central term
problems.question: An arithmetic progression has S₁₇=0. Find its first term divided by its common difference.
problems.idea: Use the arithmetic-series formula.
steps: If d≠0, divide by d to obtain a₁/d=-8.
problems.note: If d=0, the condition forces a₁=0 and the requested ratio is 0/0, undefined. The problem implicitly needs a nonzero common difference.

problems.title: Centroid and two side midpoints
problems.question: M is the centroid of ABC, and E,F are the midpoints of AB,BC. Find area ABC divided by area MEF.
problems.idea: Compare the two parallel bases and their perpendicular heights.
formulas: EF=AC/2; the centroid lies one third of the height above base AC.
steps: Let AC=b and the height from B be h. EF lies at height h/2 above AC.
M lies at height h/3, so its distance to EF is h/2-h/3=h/6.

problems.title: Translate the centre of an odd reciprocal graph
problems.question: Find the centre of symmetry of y=-1/(x+2)³-5.
problems.idea: The parent function -1/x³ is odd and centred at the origin.
formulas: An odd graph shifted by (h,k) has centre of symmetry (h,k).
steps: The x+2 shifts the graph 2 units left.
The final -5 shifts it 5 units down.

problems.title: Largest quadrilateral area with a fixed diagonal sum
problems.question: The diagonals of a quadrilateral sum to 18. Find the greatest possible area.
problems.idea: Make the diagonals perpendicular and their lengths equal.
steps: The product is at most 9·9=81, so area≤81/2=40.5.
A square with diagonals 9 attains equality.

problems.title: Circle-area ratio from equal polygon sides
problems.question: A regular hexagon and an equilateral triangle have equal side lengths. Find hexagon-incircle area divided by triangle-circumcircle area.
problems.idea: Compute the radius ratio and square it.
formulas: Hexagon inradius=s√3/2; equilateral circumradius=s/√3; circle area=πr².

problems.title: Area ratio of a triangle formed by altitude feet
problems.question: ABC is acute with C=30°. Altitudes AA₁ and BB₁ meet BC and AC. Find area A₁CB₁ divided by area ABC.
problems.idea: Both new sides next to C are projections of the corresponding old sides.
formulas: A₁C=AC cosC; B₁C=BC cosC; area ratio=cos²C.
steps: The included angle C is the same in both triangles.

problems.title: A sector-to-segment area ratio
problems.question: Find the ratio of a circle’s 60° sector area to its 90° circular-segment area.
problems.idea: Subtract the right triangle from the 90° sector.

problems.title: A parallel section halves trapezoid area
problems.question: A trapezoid has bases 3 and 6. Find the length of the parallel section dividing its area equally.
problems.idea: Extend its legs to a vertex and use areas proportional to squared parallel lengths.
formulas: Similar-triangle area ratio is the square of the side ratio.
steps: If the section length is x, the area between base 3 and section x is proportional to x²-3².
The entire trapezoid area is proportional to 6²-3².
Equal halves require x²-9=(36-9)/2, so x²=45/2.

problems.title: Count positive terms before a decreasing progression crosses zero
problems.question: An arithmetic progression has a₅=10 and a₁₁=5.8. How many terms are positive?
problems.idea: Find the common difference and solve aₙ>0 for integer n≥1.
steps: This holds for n=1,...,19; the twentieth term is negative.

problems.title: Sum the first fifty odd numbers
problems.question: cₖ=0 for even k and cₖ=k for odd k. Find the sum of the first 100 terms.
problems.idea: Only the odd-indexed terms contribute.

problems.title: Rotate around a point other than the origin
problems.question: Rotate A(3,3) clockwise by 90° about B(0,-1). Find its image.
problems.idea: Subtract the centre, rotate the displacement, then add the centre back.

problems.title: A quotient involving two quadratic roots
problems.question: If x₁,x₂ solve x²+x-1=0, evaluate $(x_1^3-x_2^3)/(1/x_1^2-1/x_2^2)$.
problems.idea: Factor both differences and use the root sum and product.
steps: The roots are distinct and nonzero, so cancellation is valid. The quotient is 2.

problems.title: Number of symmetry axes from a diagonal count
problems.question: A regular polygon has 18 more diagonals than sides. Find its number of symmetry axes.
problems.idea: Solve for its side count; a regular n-gon has n reflection axes.
steps: The positive solution is n=9, giving 9 symmetry axes.

problems.title: A reciprocal hides a sum-of-cubes factor
problems.question: Simplify $(\sqrt x+\sqrt2)^2-[(\sqrt x-\sqrt2)/(x\sqrt x-\sqrt8)]^{-1}$.
problems.idea: Use u=√x,v=√2 and factor u³-v³.
steps: The original domain is x≥0,x≠2; the denominator and numerator of the reciprocal fraction are then nonzero.
Subtract this from (u+v)²=u²+2uv+v² to obtain uv.

problems.title: At least one prepared exam ticket
problems.question: A student knows 2 of 5 mathematics tickets and 3 of 6 tickets in a second exam. Independently drawing one ticket in each exam, find the chance of getting a prepared ticket in at least one.
problems.idea: Use the complement: unprepared in both exams.
formulas: For independent draws, P(neither)=product of the two failure probabilities.
steps: Thus at least one prepared ticket has probability 1-3/10=7/10.

problems.title: Arc length from radians
problems.question: A radius-8 circle has an arc subtending 3π/4 radians. Find its length.
problems.idea: Radians make the arc-length formula direct.

problems.title: Which diagonal divides the lower trapezoid?
problems.question: A trapezoid has bases in ratio 1:2. A parallel section EF divides each leg in ratio 1:3 measured from the smaller base. In what ratio does a diagonal divide the lower trapezoid AEFD, whose base AD is larger?
problems.idea: Distinguish an original diagonal of ABCD from a diagonal of the smaller trapezoid.
formulas: Section lengths vary linearly; triangle area=base·height/2.
steps: Let the bases be b and 2b and the full height h. EF is h/4 below the smaller base, so EF=5b/4 and the lower height is 3h/4.
An original diagonal meets EF at a point dividing it into pieces 3b/4 and b/2. The triangular part in AEFD has area (1/2)(3b/4)(3h/4)=9bh/32.
The entire lower trapezoid has area (1/2)(2b+5b/4)(3h/4)=39bh/32. The other part is 30bh/32.
Thus the original diagonal gives 9:30=3:10. If “diagonal” instead means a diagonal of AEFD itself, the ratio equals its base ratio 5:8.
problems.answer: 3:10 for an original diagonal of ABCD; 5:8 for AEFD’s own diagonal.
problems.note: The wording does not name the diagonal’s endpoints. The listed 3:10 uses the original trapezoid diagonal.

problems.title: Compute a dot product after vector arithmetic
problems.question: a=(-3,6),b=(3,-2). Find (a-2b)·(a+b).
problems.idea: Compute the two vectors first.

problems.title: A 5-12-13 triangle from a radius difference
problems.question: A right triangle’s leg ratio is 2.4. Its circumradius exceeds its inradius by 9 dm. Find its area.
problems.idea: The side ratio is 5:12:13.
steps: Write the legs as 5t,12t and hypotenuse as 13t.
Then R=13t/2 and r=2t, so R-r=9t/2=9.
Thus t=2, and the legs are 10 and 24.

problems.title: An acute vector angle requires a positive dot product
problems.question: For which k do a=(-3,k) and b=(0,-1) form an acute angle?
problems.idea: Both vectors are nonzero, so the dot-product sign determines the angle type.

problems.title: Area of a square in a dodecagon’s circumcircle
problems.question: A regular dodecagon inscribed in a circle has area 18√2 cm². Find the area of a square inscribed in the same circle.
problems.idea: Express both areas through the common circumradius.
formulas: Regular n-gon area=(n/2)R²sin(360°/n); inscribed square area=2R².
steps: For n=12, the polygon area is 6R²sin30°=3R².
problems.note: None of the listed choices equals 12√2. The printed dodecagon area contains the factor √2, so it cannot be dropped.

problems.title: Geometric probability inside a circumdisk
problems.question: Choose a point uniformly inside the disk circumscribed about an equilateral triangle. Find the probability that it lies inside the triangle.
problems.idea: Divide the triangle area by the disk area.
formulas: For circumradius R, equilateral area=3√3R²/4; disk area=πR².
steps: The favourable region is the entire equilateral triangle.
problems.note: This is uniform selection inside the disk, as stated in the printed question. Selection only on the circumference would instead have probability zero for the triangle interior.

problems.title: Reflection of the origin in a line
problems.question: Find the point symmetric to the origin about 3x+4y=12.
problems.idea: The perpendicular direction is the line’s normal vector (3,4).

problems.title: Area from the intercepts of an absolute quadratic
problems.question: Find the area of the axis-intercept triangle of y=-|x²-5x+6|+3.
problems.idea: Find all x-intercepts and the y-intercept.
steps: At y=0, the positive case gives x²-5x+3=0, with roots (5±√13)/2. Their separation is √13.
The negative case gives x²-5x+9=0, with negative discriminant, so there are no additional intercepts.
